topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's welcome, course context, and outline of learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: bad luck, genetics, and environmental exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contributing factors to cancer development, balancing endogenous random mutations and genetic predispositions against environmental risks supported by epidemiological and population data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and biological carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, radiation, and non-mutagenic promoters initiate and drive tumor formation.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological tools used to demonstrate that specific agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with overarching takeaways on lifestyle risks, regulatory challenges, and daily risk-benefit decisions.
